title: Cash when you need it
blurb: How fast, and at what cost, things turn back into cash, and why growth is not the only thing to compare.
t1.title: Turning things into cash
t1.hook: Dev needs cash within a week for a sudden repair bill. Your mission: find out how quickly his money can become cash.
t1.define: **Liquidity** is how fast and how cheaply you can turn something into cash.
t1.analogy: A bag of rice sells in minutes at the market. A house can take weeks or months to find a buyer.
q1.opt.a: How fast and how cheaply you can turn something into cash
q1.opt.c: How much tax you pay on it
q1.hint: Think of the rice and the house.
q1.explain: Liquidity is about speed and cost of getting cash, not about growth.
q2.opt.a: Money in the Steady Box, which sells in about a day
q2.opt.b: A plot of land, which can take months to sell
q2.hint: Which one turns into cash faster?
q2.explain: The Steady Box turns into cash in about a day. Land takes far longer.
t2.title: Check the speed
t2.define: Getting cash has two prices: the time it takes, and the cost of selling. Both vary a lot from one asset to another.
t2.explore: Open the lab with {amt}. Try each place and compare the days and the cost.
q3.prompt: In the lab, how many rupees does it cost to sell the Bumpy Ride holding? Type a number in rupees.
q3.hint: Read the cost of selling in the lab.
q4.prompt: If Dev sells the property, how much cash lands in his hand? Type a number in rupees.
q4.hint: Read the cash in your hand in the lab.
q4.explain: Selling property costs {propSell}. Of {amt}, Dev keeps {propGot}.
q5.prompt: Which of these takes the longest to turn into cash?
q5.hint: Compare the days in the lab.
q5.explain: Property takes about three months, far longer than the others.
t3.title: A deadline test
t3.hook: Dev needs {amt} in 10 days. Most of his savings sit in property.
t3.define: When you need cash soon, slow and costly choices are the risky ones, even if they might grow well.
q6.prompt: Can Dev's property deliver the cash in 10 days?
q6.opt.a: Probably not, because a property sale takes far longer
q6.opt.b: Yes, property always sells in a week
q6.opt.c: Yes, because property is the most liquid
q6.opt.d: It does not matter how long it takes
q6.hint: Check the days for property in the lab.
q6.explain: A property sale takes about three months, so 10 days is too short.
q7.prompt: If Dev held gold instead, selling costs {goldSell}. On {amt}, how many rupees go to that cost? Type a number in rupees.
q7.hint: The selling cost rate times the amount.
t4.title: Safety, access, growth
t4.define: Every asset trades off three things: **safety** (does it hold its value), **access** (how fast you can get cash) and **growth**. None wins all three.
t4.tradeoff: The right mix depends on when you will need the money. Cash needed soon wants access. Cash that can wait can lean on growth.
q8.prompt: Asha says: pick whatever has the highest growth. What is she missing?
q8.opt.a: Whether she can get cash when she needs it, and how big the swings are
q8.opt.b: Nothing, the highest growth is always best
q8.opt.c: Growth does not matter at all
q8.opt.d: Only the colour of the logo
q8.fb.b: Highest growth often comes with big swings and slow access. It is one thing to compare, not the only thing.
q8.hint: Reread the three things every asset trades off.
q8.explain: Growth is one of three things. Access and safety matter too.
q9.prompt: Property in Dev's town rose last year. What can you say?
q9.opt.a: It can also stay flat or fall, and it is slow and costly to sell
q9.opt.d: It can be sold in a day at no cost
q9.fb.b: Property does not always rise. It can stay flat or fall, and selling costs time and money.
q9.hint: Think about the days and the cost you saw in the lab.
q9.explain: A rise last year promises nothing, and selling property is slow and costly.
glossary.sell_cost.def: What it costs, in rupees, to turn something into cash.
